sessions.name: A
sessions.reply:
For an empty store, `list` prints nothing and exits with code 0.

I ran `python -m fieldnotes.cli list` with `NOTES_HOME` set to a new, empty temp directory:

```
$ NOTES_HOME=<empty tmp dir> python -m fieldnotes.cli list
$ echo $?
0
```

There is no "no notes" message. `store.load()` returns `[]` when `notes.json` doesn't exist, so the list loop in `fieldnotes/cli.py` has nothing to print. The run also didn't create `notes.json`. Only `add` writes it.

I haven't saved your note about `notes.json` and `NOTES_HOME` anywhere. This project has no CLAUDE.md, and the Recalith hooks only record what I observe during a task. I can add a CLAUDE.md with that line if you want it kept.

actions.command: cd <run>/work/R4/c/w && export NOTES_HOME="$(mktemp -d)" && echo "before:" && python tools/count_notes.py && python -m fieldnotes.cli add "first" && python -m fieldnotes.cli add "second" && echo "after:" && python tools/count_notes.py && rm -r "$NOTES_HOME"

sessions.name: C
sessions.reply:
I added `tools/count_notes.py`, which prints the number of stored notes by calling `store.load()`. It reads from `NOTES_HOME`, so that variable has to be set.

I tested it against a temporary `NOTES_HOME` directory. It printed 0 before. I then added two notes with `python -m fieldnotes.cli add`, and it printed 2. I deleted the temp directory afterward, so your real notes are untouched.

The project memory says notes live in `notes.json`, but `fieldnotes/store.py` actually uses `notes.jsonl`. I followed the code. That memory entry looks stale.
